statement: Fix a0 < π and b0 < ∞, and let η = a + ib1 satisfy |a| ≤ a0, |b1| ≤ b0. The following bounds hold uniformly for admissible real parts of α, with the imaginary fields specified below. In parts 1–3, h > 0 is fixed and sufficiently small. 1. If M is real and z = 0, then for sufficiently small fixed h > 0, with no truncation of the explicit counts, A ≥ cB(x) − ChL − Chne. 2. Suppose ne is polynomially bounded, and that pL has the properties stated above. For any v = Im M ∈ R and any j ∈ Z, the choice zσ = −σvpL gives A ≥ cB(x) − ChL − Chne + 2πjv − Ch (︁ v2 + (1 + f)|v| )︁ . There is no polynomial restriction on j in this estimate. 3. Suppose in addition that |j| is polynomially bounded. There are a value v = Im M, independent of Re M, and an imaginary field z with the required totals such that A ≥ cB(x) + cδU2 L − ChL − Chne. The value v is polynomially bounded. Each zσ + σvpL is the derivative of a smooth primitive supported in |u| ≤ (1 − δ/2)L, with polynomial bounds on all required fixed-order derivatives. Moreover, the number of far particles in [−(1 − 2δ)L, (1 − 2δ)L] is at most CU for large L. 4. Under the same polynomial hypotheses, suppose U ≤ U0. Choose a desired error ε > 0, then h sufficiently small, then δ sufficiently small. The constant U0 may be fixed arbitrarily after these choices. There are a value v = Im M, independent of Re M, and an imaginary field z, with the same support and polynomial regularity properties as in part 3, such that A ≥ c′ εB(x) + 2L Re(η2) 4κ − CεL − o(L) − Chne. The selected v is polynomially bounded. The retained coefficient c′ ε > 0 can be taken independent of δ, U0. On these bounded-U configurations, integrating the explicit factorial measures with the factor exp(Chne), while using a fixed portion of the retained B(x)-damping, costs at most exp (︁ Ch,εδL + o(L) )︁ . The same conclusion allows further fixed exponential factors per explicit particle after reducing δ as needed. 34 The constants are uniform once the polynomial bounds and the previously fixed parameters are fixed. In part 4 the asymptotic limit is taken only after ε, h, δ, U0 have been chosen in that order; constants depending on those fixed choices are allowed in o(L).
